name: AniList
tagline: Anime, manga, characters, users, lists, and activity through GraphQL.
description: AniList's GraphQL API lets agents search public anime, manga, character, staff, and user data. OAuth unlocks private user data and mutations such as updating media lists.

methods.label: OAuth 2.0
methods.note: Required for private data and all mutations.

auth.guide:
**Public queries (fastest):** send GraphQL POST requests without a credential for public anime, manga, character, staff, and user data:

```bash
curl https://graphql.anilist.co \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"query { Media(id: 1) { id title { romaji } } }"}'
```

**OAuth token (mutations and private data):** register an application in AniList developer settings, complete the authorization-code or implicit flow, and send the resulting access token as a Bearer credential:

```bash
curl https://graphql.anilist.co \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANILIST_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"query { Viewer { id name } }"}'
```

AniList does not support OAuth scopes; its access tokens are long-lived and currently have no refresh tokens. Official docs explicitly say public data needs no authentication, private data and data mutation do, and all mutations require authentication.

interfaces.name: AniList GraphQL API
interfaces.note: Public queries work unauthenticated, while all mutations and access to private user data require an OAuth access token.
